questions.question: Antibiotics are NOT effective on a virus as a virus lacks _____.

__
 
• Antibiotics are not effective on a virus as it lacks a cell wall.
 
• **How antibiotics work**
 
 
• They are used to t**reat infections caused by bacteria**.
 
• There ar**e two types** of antibiotics that work to stop bacterial infections.
 
• Some slow down the growth of bacteria and damage their ability to reproduce and spread.
 
• While others kill the bacteria by destroying the** bacteria cell walls.** The choice of antibiotic depends on the type of bacteria.

questions.question: When a body rolls over the surface of another body, the resistance to its motion is called _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**rolling friction**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• For a moving solid body, there are **2 principal types** of friction are following

 
 
• **Rolling friction**
 
• **Sliding friction**
 
 
 
• On a surface, The force resisting the motion of a rolling body is known as** Rolling resistance or Rolling friction**.
 
 
• The **Rolling of a wheel or ball** on the ground is an **example **of Rolling friction.
 
 
 
• In **Sliding friction**, there is a restriction on the movement of the body as only one side of the body is in contact with the surface.
 
 
• An **example **of Sliding friction is **Pushing a box across the table**.
 
 
 
• Rolling resistance** **is weaker than **sliding friction**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• When 2 surfaces are rubbed against each other, **Sliding friction** takes place.
 
• When an object rolls on the surface, **Rolling friction** takes place.
 
• Because of rolling friction, **A basketball rolled on the court will eventually come to a halt**.
 
• **A broad tire bike will burn extra fuel** because of the increased Rolling friction.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is **NOT **true about Ashokan pillars?

options.text: These are said to be monolithic pillars.
Ashoka got the inspiration for such pillars from his father Bindusar.
These were usually made of sandstone.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ashoka got the inspiration for such pillars from his father Bindusar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Characteristics of Ashokan pillars are**

 
 
• Ashoka got the inspiration for such pillars from **Persians and the Greeks.**
 
• They were generally monolithic and were made up of sandstone.
 
• They were polished pillars like the **Lion Capital of Ashoka from Sarnath. **
 
• The similarity of architecture suggests that they were all sculpted by craftsmen from the same region.
 
• The** pillars have four component parts in two pieces.**
 
• **The three sections** of the capitals are made in a single piece, often of a different stone to that of the **monolithic shaft** to which they are attached by a **large metal dowel.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Ashoka pillars** are a **series of columns dispersed throughout the Indian subcontinent**.
 
• The Mauryan Empire Ashoka used the expression **Dhaṃma thaṃbha "pillars of the Dharma" to describe his own pillars**.
 
• The Ashoka's pillars are among the **earliest known stone sculptural remains from India.**
 
• All Ashoka's pillars were built at **Buddhist monasteries, many important sites from the life of the Buddha and places of pilgrimage**.
 
• Some **pillars **were erected to commemorate** visits by Ashoka**.

questions.question: Which of the following Sultans of Delhi was the first one to start military campaigns in southern India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Alauddin Khilji**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Alauddin Khilji **was an emperor of the Khalji dynasty and he ruled the Delhi Sultanate.
 
• Alauddin Khalji reign from **1296 to 1316**.
 
• Khalji is noted for repulsing the **Mongol invasions of India**.
 
• During **1310-1311**, the Delhi Sultanate ruler **Alauddin Khalji **sent an army led by **Malik Kafur** to the southernmost kingdoms of India.
 
• After subjugating the **Hoysalas, Malik Kafur invaded the Pandya kingdom** in present-day Tamil Nadu, taking advantage of a war of succession between the **Pandya brothers Vira and Sundara**.
 
• **During March–April 1311**, he raided several places in the Pandya territory, including their capital **Madurai**.
 
• He was unable to make the Pandya king a tributary to the Delhi Sultanate but obtained huge plunder, including elephants, horses, gold, and precious stones.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Alauddin **Khilji was a nephew and a son-in-law of his predecessor Jalaluddin.
 
• After killing **Jalaluddin**, Khilji consolidated his power in Delhi and subjugated Jalaluddin's sons in Multan.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles was deleted by the Constitution (Forty-Fourth Amendment) Act, 1978?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 31**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 31** is being deleted by the** Forty-Fourth Amendment Act, of 1978.**
 
• 44th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted as The Constitution (44th Amendment) Act, 1978.
 
• This amendment says that the **‘Right to property under Article 31 of the Constitution is removed from the fundamental rights and is made a legal right.**
 
• This act was passed in 1978 by the Morarji Desai government **who served between 1977 and 1979 as the 4th Prime Minister of India.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• 44th Amendment made a few changes in the provisions of the constitution. They are given in points below:
 
• Any changes in the basic structure of the constitution can be made only if they are approved by the people of India by a majority of votes at a referendum in which at least fifty-one per cent of the electorate participated.
 
 
• **Article 368 is being amended to ensure this.**
 
 
 
• The 44th Amendment Act of 1978 reversed the provision made by the 42nd amendment act that allowed the government to amend the constitution on its wish by Article 368.
 
 
• 44th Amendment Act nullified this unjustified power to the government.
 
 
 
• The right to Property was removed from the list of fundamental rights (Article 31) and was made a legal right under Article 300A.
 
• Proclamation of Emergency can be issued only when the security of India or any part of its territory is threatened by war or external aggression or by armed rebellion.
 
 
• Internal disturbance not amounting to armed rebellion would not be a ground for the issue of a Proclamation.
 
 
 
• An emergency can be proclaimed only on the basis of written advice tendered to the President by the Cabinet.
 
• The right to liberty is further strengthened by the provision that the law for preventive detention cannot authorise, in any case, detention for a longer period than three months, unless an Advisory Board has reported that there is sufficient cause for such detention.
 
• Right of the media to report freely and without censorship the proceedings in Parliament and the State Legislatures.

questions.question: When a chemical, which is basic in nature, is treated with turmeric paste, it turns ______ in colour.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**red**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Turmeric is an acid-base indicator
 
 
• Turmeric compound remains **yellow when acid or neutral solutions are added to it**.
 
• When **basic solutions **such as sodium hydroxide are added to it, the solution turns** pinkish-red.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Turmeric is a flowering plant, **Curcuma longa** of the ginger family, **Zingiberaceae**.
 
• Turmeric is a r**hizomatous, perennial, herbaceous plant** native to the **Indian subcontinent and Southeast **Asia.
 
• It requires a considerable amount of annual **rainfall **to thrive and **temperatures **between** 20 and 30 °C**.
 
• Turmeric powder has a** bitter, warm, black pepper–like flavor and earthy, mustard-like aroma**.
 
• A bright yellow chemical produced by the turmeric plant is **Curcumin**.
 
• **Curcumin **is approved as a **food additive** by the **European Parliament, WHO, and United States Food and Drug Administration**.
 
• It is long used in Ayurvedic medicine, where it is also known as **Haridra**.
 
• **Turmeric **is commonly used in **Indian clothing, like saris and Buddhist monks' robes**.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a fundamental duty of the citizens of India as specified in Part IV-A of the constitution of India?

• In North India, the betimes use of the term in a similar sense was in Bengal in the Barabar Hill Cave Inscription of the Maukhari Chief, Anantavarman in which his father is described as the Samanta-Chudamanih of the imperial Guptas.

questions.question: The landform named ‘meander’ is created by a ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**river.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The landform named **‘meander’ is created by a river.**
 
• A** meander is a winding curve** or twist in a river.
 
• They are typically** found in the middle and inferior course** of a river.
 
• This is due to the vertical erosion is **substituted by a sideways form of erosion called lateral erosion,** plus deposition within the floodplain.
 
• A meander is one of a category of** steady sinuous curves, bends, loops, turns, or windings in the channel of a river, stream**, or another watercourse.
 
• It is generated by a stream or river swinging from** side to side as it flows across its floodplain** or shifts its channel within a valley.
 
• A meander is generated by a stream or river as it erodes the sediments including an outer,** concave bank (cut bank), and deposits this and other sediments downstream on an inner, convex bank which is typically a point bar.**

questions.question: Of the following Harappan Civilization sites, which one provides the evidence of a large open area with terraced stands, identified as ‘stadium’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dholavira.**__

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• The evidence of a** large open area with terraced stands,** identified as ‘stadium’ was found at **Dholavira.**
 
• The City of Dholavira is situated in **Khadir island of the Rann of Kutch **belonged to matured Harappan phase.
 
• Today it is seen as a** fortified quadrangular city set in a **harsh arid land, was once a thriving **metropolis for 1200 years (3000 BCE-1800 BCE), **and had an access to the sea prior to a decrease in sea level.
 
• Dholavira was founded in **1968-68 by architect J.P. Joshi.**
 
• It was the** fifth largest site** among the 8 major sites discovered during the Harappan Civilization.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The excavation revealed the** urban planning and architecture and unearthed large numbers** of old materials such as **animal bones, gold, silver, terracotta ornaments, pottery, and bronze vessels.**
 
• Archaeologists believed that **Dholavira** was a vital center of trade between settlements in **south Gujarat, Sindh, and Punjab, and Western Asia.**
